name: the-desk
title: A Person Asks the Release Desk
part: The release, in the order it runs
html:
A Person Asks the Release Desk

One Act

desk:release: which pull request.

It Speaks HEART

The same media type as the library, and as HTML for a person.

ARTIE Takes Over

The desk starts ARTIE on the kept release script.
say: A release starts with a person, at the release desk. The desk is a small service, and it speaks HEART, the same as the library: here it is in a browser, as plain HTML, because a HEART service can answer a person too. Its one act: release a pull request. Fill in which one, and send. The desk hands the job to ARTIE, running the kept release script. From here on, ARTIE drives, and every step it takes is something the last answer offered. First stop: the forge, to open the pull request.

deck:ref.label: HEART
deck:ref.title: HEART: one media type, information and controls together
deck:ref.summary: Hypermedia Enforced Agentic Reliable Transactions. HAL with HAL Schema Forms, plus a small profile. Every answer carries the resource's data and the forms for the acts its state allows now, each with a method, an address and a JSON Schema; an act that isn't offered can say why (hr:unavailable).

deck:ref.name: artie
deck:ref.label: ARTIE
deck:ref.title: ARTIE: the generic client
deck:ref.summary: Autonomous Restful Traversal and Interactive Engine. Coupled to HEART and HTTP, and to nothing about any one API, as a browser is to HTML. It enters by a bookmark, checks a kept script's pins against what is offered, sends each act with its If-Match validator, and caches forms and schemas (L2).
